To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Orion A giant molecular cloud has a complex structure and kinematics, with possible external triggers of star formation, including collisions with the diffuse gas and the effects of UV radiation.

we have found two types of external triggering mechanisms in the Orion A GMC: (1) collision of the diffuse gas with the surface of a dense molecular cloud, and (2) irradiation of UV on pre-existing filaments or molecular cloud cores.

we have found that there are two types of possible external triggers of star formation in the northern part of Orion A GMC, which are 1) collision of the diffuse gas with the cloud surface and 2) irradiation of UV on pre-existing filaments, and that the wide and high-sensitivity images of the Orion A GMC have provided the first panoramic view of the possible sites of triggered star-formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of stars in the Orion-A molecular cloud.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Orion-A GMC is in an active stage of forming stars in various environments, and that the star formation is triggered by the collision of the diffuse gas with the GMC and by the UV irradiation from the nearby massive stars.
the star formation in the northern part of Orion-A GMC is triggered by the combination of the collision of the diffuse gas with the GMC and the irradiation of UV radiation from nearby O stars.
the Orion-A GMC is currently in a transition phase from the collapse of the pre-existing filamental structure to the triggered star formation by external forces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the star formation in the OMC-1 region is mainly driven by the gravitational contraction of the molecular cloud, and those of the OMC2/3 and OMC-4 regions are mainly triggered by the collision of the molecular cloud with the diffuse gas and/or the irradiation of UV from OMC-1.
the star formation activity in the Orion-A cloud is triggered by both internal and external forces.

the OMC-1 and OMC-2 regions are the most active sites of star formation in the GMC, and that the star-formation activities are triggered by external forces, i.e., collision of the diffuse gas and irradiation of UV, at the surface of the OMCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
star formation in the GMC is triggered not only by internal processes but also by external processes.
the Orion-A GMC is a very active site of triggered star formation.
the external forces, such as the collision of diffuse gas and UV irradiation, are important for triggering star formation in the GMCs.
